projectName: Meridian Payments Autonomous Report Reliability Platform

services.name: Report Reliability API
services.description: Spring Boot REST API and reliability engine for classifying job attempts, detecting undelivered reports, executing bounded retries, auditing outcomes, and exposing operational metrics.

questions.question: Which language should the Report Reliability API use?

options.label: Java
options.description: Java 21, as specified by the Meridian technical requirements.

questions.question: Which framework should the Report Reliability API use?

options.label: Spring Boot 3
options.description: Spring Boot 3.x, as specified by the Meridian technical requirements.

options.label: Other JVM framework
options.description: Choose another JVM framework if the mandated stack should be changed.

questions.rationale: The case study mandates Spring Boot 3.x, Maven, Spring Data JPA, Spring Retry, Lombok, and Jakarta Validation.

questions.question: What capabilities should the Report Reliability API provide?
questions.recommendedChoice: Configurable status classification; detect undelivered reports grouped by tenant, report, and schedule; retry only retryable failures with a maximum of three retries; persist retry history and audit events; expose operational metrics and the specified REST endpoints; provide SQL/CSV/JSON sample data, tests, Docker assets, README, and solution design documentation.
questions.answer: Configurable status classification; detect undelivered reports grouped by tenant, report, and schedule; retry only retryable failures with a maximum of three retries; persist retry history and audit events; expose operational metrics and the specified REST endpoints; provide SQL/CSV/JSON sample data, tests, Docker assets, README, and solution design documentation.
questions.rationale: These capabilities are explicitly required in Meridian_Agent.md.

questions.question: Which data stores does the application need?

options.label: MySQL
options.description: Persist job attempts, configurable classification rules, retry history, audit events, and operationally useful data.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Choose only if the application requires no persistence.

questions.rationale: MySQL and durable storage for classification rules, attempts, retry history, and audits are explicit requirements.

questions.question: Do users need to sign in to use the application's API features?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Require users to sign in to use application API features.

options.label: No
options.description: No user sign-in requirement is specified for the API features.

questions.rationale: The case study specifies service APIs and operational controls but does not require end-user sign-in; authentication can be added as a future security hardening decision.
